note: Fixed question set. Do not edit between runs: comparability depends on it. key_facts is a checklist for human review only; no script grades against it.

questions.q: When does retrieval-augmented generation beat fine-tuning, and when does it not?
key_facts: RAG wins when knowledge changes faster than retraining
RAG wins when answers need source attribution
FT wins for stable domain behaviour and tone
FT wins when latency matters or offline is required
Hybrid often outperforms both

questions.q: How should a RAG system be evaluated in production?
key_facts: Faithfulness or groundedness is a primary metric
Answer relevancy measures whether the answer addresses the question
Context precision and recall are separate concerns
Retrieval quality must be measured independently of generation

questions.q: What is hybrid search and what does it actually improve over pure vector search?
key_facts: Hybrid combines lexical and dense retrieval
BM25 or similar catches exact terms and rare identifiers
Dense vectors handle paraphrase
Reciprocal rank fusion or score blending combines the two

questions.q: What causes hallucinations in retrieval-augmented generation?
key_facts: Poor retrieval returns irrelevant context
The model over-relies on context it cannot verify
Context conflicts with parametric knowledge
Long noisy contexts degrade grounding

questions.q: What is reciprocal rank fusion and when is it used?
key_facts: RRF combines rankings from several retrievers
It uses rank position rather than raw scores
No score normalisation between retrievers is needed
Used in hybrid search systems

questions.q: How are documents chunked for retrieval, and what chunk size works best?
key_facts: Chunks are sized in tokens not characters
Too small loses context, too large dilutes embeddings
Overlapping chunks reduce boundary loss
Chunk size is task and model dependent

questions.q: What is the difference between context precision and context recall?
key_facts: Precision is the share of retrieved context that is relevant
Recall is the share of relevant context that was retrieved
High recall low precision wastes context window
They trade off and should be measured separately

questions.q: How does query expansion or sub-query decomposition affect retrieval quality?
key_facts: Decomposition targets one facet per sub-query
Multi-hop questions need sequential retrieval
Expansion increases recall and cost
Naive expansion can add noise

questions.q: What is the private internal revenue of a specific unnamed enterprise using this system last quarter?
questions.expected: Should say the sources are insufficient, not invent a figure.

questions.q: What will the exact retrieval accuracy benchmark be for a model released next year?
questions.expected: Should refuse to predict a specific number.

questions.q: What is the source code of the retriever implementation used to build this report?
questions.expected: Should state this cannot be found in web sources.

questions.q: Since retrieval-augmented generation was shown to eliminate hallucinations entirely, what is the residual error rate?
questions.expected: Should reject the premise that RAG eliminates hallucination, then answer the real question.

questions.q: How much faster is BM25 than dense retrieval, given that BM25 uses transformers internally?
questions.expected: Should correct the premise; BM25 is lexical, not transformer-based.

questions.q: Does adding a reranker to a RAG pipeline improve or degrade end-to-end accuracy?
questions.expected: Sources may conflict. Report both positions rather than picking one.

questions.q: Is a larger context window a substitute for better retrieval?
questions.expected: Sources may conflict. Report both positions rather than picking one.
